findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~90 — parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse result wrapper ({success, data}) which is assigned directly to key and persisted via prisma.credential.update, so every Google token refresh stores the wrapper as the credential key; on next load googleCredentialSchema parsing fails and the integration breaks. It must persist key.data (after the success check), not the wrapper.

[High/bug] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-10 — the computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (the second overwrites the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema actually only requires access_token; the intended "any numeric property is the expiry" validation never happens, so sync responses missing the expiry pass validation and propagate undefined expiry dates downstream.

[High/bug] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:14-21 — in sync mode the function returns a raw fetch Response (never .json()-parsed, no response.ok check), but callers expect provider-specific shapes: Google does res?.data then token.access_token (throws on undefined), Zoho Bigin/CRM access tokenInfo.data.error on undefined (throws), and Hubspot reads .refresh_token/.expires_in off a Response (undefined → NaN expiry persisted). The sync path is broken for these integrations.

[High/security] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:14-19 — the outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication at all (no secret header, unlike the inbound webhook), and calcomUserId is a sequential enumerable ID, so anyone who can reach the endpoint can obtain fresh OAuth access tokens for arbitrary users.

[High/data] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:24-26 — when the response lacks refresh_token, the literal string "refresh_token" is injected into the parsed data and then persisted by callers (office365calendar CalendarService spreads tokenResponse.data over o365AuthCredentials before saving; zoom stores parsedToken.data), permanently overwriting the user's real refresh token and making the credential unusable if sync is later disabled or the local refresh path is used.

[High/data] packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~90 — when the sync env vars are set, parseRefreshTokenResponse uses the minimum schema and zod's default unknown-key stripping reduces the full Salesforce token response to just access_token; the code then persists {...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token} as the entire credential key, silently dropping instance_url, signature, scope, token_type, id, issued_at from the stored credential.

[Medium/security] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:19-23 — the webhook secret is compared with plain !== rather than a constant-time comparison (crypto.timingSafeEqual), leaving a timing side-channel for recovering CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET.

[Medium/concurrency] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:63-87 — the findFirst → update/create sequence is a check-then-act race: two concurrent webhook calls for the same (userId, appId) can both find nothing and both create, producing duplicate credentials; additionally, findFirst without orderBy is nondeterministic when duplicates already exist.

[Medium/bug] packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:~85 — credentialId (the credential's ID) is passed as the userId parameter of refreshOAuthTokens, so in sync mode the sync endpoint receives the credential ID as calcomUserId and resolves the wrong user (or none).

[Medium/bug] packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~80 — response.statusText !== "OK" is an unreliable success check: statusText is empty for HTTP/2 responses and can be altered by proxies, causing spurious 400s. Use response.ok/response.status instead.

[Medium/performance] packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~75-95 — the service performs a Salesforce token-refresh HTTP call plus a prisma.credential.update write on every instantiation, with no expiry check, adding a network round-trip and DB write to every calendar operation and risking provider rate limits.

[Medium/api] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:26 — appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) throws an unhandled ZodError (as do the unguarded symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse calls), so malformed payloads surface as 500s instead of 400s; use safeParse and return a 4xx.

[Low/api] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:13 — the handler never checks req.method, so any HTTP method is processed (e.g., a GET hits the body parse and 500s); it should reject non-POST with 405.

[Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:19-21 — CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME is not lowercased before the req.headers lookup; Node lowercases header keys, so any uppercase character in the env value silently fails authentication with 403. The code should apply .toLowerCase() instead of relying on the .env.example comment.

[Low/bug] packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~75 — the Salesforce token refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely, so credential-sync deployments cannot refresh Salesforce tokens through the sync endpoint, inconsistent with every other integration wired in this PR.

[Low/doc_defect] .env.example:~240 — the key "must be 32 bytes" for AES256, but the suggested openssl rand -base64 24 generates 24 bytes (32 base64 characters); if the key is base64-decoded before use it is an invalid AES-256 key length, and if used raw it has only 192 bits of entropy. The doc and the stated requirement contradict each other.

[Medium/test_gap] No tests were added for the new webhook handler (app-credential.ts), refreshOAuthTokens, or parseRefreshTokenResponse — security-sensitive authentication, decryption, and token-refresh logic ships completely untested.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-10 — the computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (the second overwrites the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema actually only requires access_token; the intended "any numeric property is the expiry" validation never happens, so sync responses missing the expiry pass validation and propagate undefined expiry dates downstream.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS, `z.string().toString()` yields a plain string key (not a dynamic “any string key” constraint), and both expressions will evaluate to the same string (e.g. "[object Object]"), so the latter property overwrites the former in the object literal. As a result, the schema does not enforce “any numeric property” (expiry) at all—effectively only `access_token` is required—so responses without an expiry field can pass validation and propagate undefined expiry values downstream.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Cal.com will `POST` to the configured endpoint with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication material (no shared-secret header, signature, or token). Given the feature’s intent (getting fresh OAuth tokens “for” a user), this is a security defect in the introduced design because the request provides no way for the receiving service to verify it came from Cal.com, and it relies on an enumerable `userId` identifier.

Also, using `findFirst` without an `orderBy` means if duplicates already exist, which record gets updated is nondeterministic.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the `handler` processes all requests without checking `req.method`. It always runs header/secret validation and then `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`. For non-POST methods (e.g., GET), `req.body` may be missing/empty, causing Zod `.parse` to throw and (absent a try/catch) likely result in a 500 instead of a proper 405. The finding is directly supported by the diff: there is no method guard anywhere in the handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:19-21 — CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME is not lowercased before the req.headers lookup; Node lowercases header keys, so any uppercase character in the env value silently fails authentication with 403. The code should apply .toLowerCase() instead of relying on the .env.example comment.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the header lookup uses req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]. In Node/Next, incoming request header keys are normalized to lowercase on req.headers, so if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME is configured with any uppercase characters, this property access won’t match and the secret check will always fail, returning 403.
